l'ouverture: And when he was older and came to know of Frederick Douglass and Toussaint L’Ouverture, he knew if he could but burst his bonds he, too, could write his name in glory.

His oration was Wendell Phillips's "Toussaint L'Ouverture," a speech which may now be classed as rhetorical--even, perhaps, bombastic; but as the words fell from "Shiny's" lips their effect was magical.

When, in the famous peroration, his voice, trembling with suppressed emotion, rose higher and higher and then rested on the name "Toussaint L'Ouverture," it was like touching an electric button which loosed the pent-up feelings of his listeners.

l'observatoire: Left alone at the flat in the Avenue de l’Observatoire she would dine in the Rue St Jacques and go for solitary walks when the meal was over.
Often during these walks she passed under the windows of the studio in the Avenue de l’Observatoire.
For he could so easily say--he often did say--‘Why did you leave the Avenue de l’Observatoire?’

They passed the deserted entrance of the Bal Bullier and the coloured lights of the Closerie des Lilas, and crossed the street into the dimness of the Avenue de l’Observatoire, where the tops of the trees vanished, ghostlike, in the mist.
It was late when she got back to the Avenue de l’Observatoire.
